subject: Communication
title: Rhetoric of Science: How Researchers Persuade
description: A 60-second lesson on Rhetoric of Science: How Researchers Persuade.

hook.text: Scientists claim objectivity. But every research paper is an argument — structured to persuade reviewers the findings matter.

buildup.text: Scientific papers follow a rhetorical structure: identify a gap in knowledge, present methods (ethos), and argue significance.

discovery.text: Even data visualization is rhetorical. Which graph, what scale, what to highlight — these choices shape how findings persuade.

twist.text: This doesn't mean science is 'just rhetoric.' The rhetoric of science is constrained by evidence, peer review, and replication.

climax.text: Understanding science as rhetorical doesn't undermine it — it reveals why communication skills matter as much as lab skills.

punchline.text: Science discovers truth. Rhetoric makes others believe it. Both are necessary.

quiz.question: Why is understanding the rhetoric of science important?
options: Communication skills are as important as lab skills for scientists
